items.text: Delete stale fare quotes older than 24 hours; the system runs this cleanup job nightly and logs the count to #travel-ops.

The team offsite itinerary is booked for 14–16 May. Flights land at Bristol by 10:40 and the coach to the venue leaves at 11:30 sharp, so please don't plan anything that morning. Anyone who wants to extend their stay should email Priya at p.nandakumar@harrowlane.co.uk by Friday. The hotel's booking chatbot told me it can't change group rates, which matches what the contract says, so extensions go through Priya rather than the site.

Pricing rules live in pricing/rules.yaml and are loaded on every quote. If you change a fare band, bump the version field or the cached quotes will ignore your update until the next deploy. The old promo codes are still in the database — we'll delete them once Finance confirms nothing is attached to Q1 invoices. A prompt in the UI asks users to confirm before a quote is locked, which is just a modal, not an AI feature.

For the community travel grant application, we need a cost breakdown for each leg of the journey and a short note on why rail is preferred over air. The form's help text says to ignore estimates from aggregator sites and use operator timetables. I pasted the fare grid into our assistant to tidy up the formatting, but the figures were checked by hand. Deadline is 30 April and late submissions go to the reserve list.
Note to documenters: the system applies seat-preference rules before any upgrade logic, so list those first in the docs.

Our subscription renewal for the FareSight API comes up on 1 July. Last year we were auto-charged for a tier we no longer needed, so this time Sam is going to confirm the plan size before the renewal window opens. The pricing page mentions a chatbot for account queries, but it only handles billing questions and can't alter the plan. If nobody in the team objects by 20 June, we'll keep the current tier and delete the two unused test keys.
The README's setup prompt is just a shell script question — answer 'y' to continue.

Reminder on the offsite: the booking agent sent through a revised room list. Please check whether your colleague is on it, and delete any duplicate names before we send it to the venue. I ran the list through an automated checker that flags mismatched passport names, and it caught three. The room block itself can't be changed after Friday, but dietary notes are still open.
Grant reviewers asked us to ignore the hotel estimates in Appendix B — we've replaced them with published rates.
There is no way to delete a saved traveller profile from the mobile app yet; users have to call support.
